protocol: MyChron5/6 WiFi download protocol (clean-room observation, issue 6.2)
source: AiM iOS app <-> MyChron6 (fw 02.46.16), captured via pymobiledevice3 pcapd; raw .pcapng kept local only

checksum.name: stcp_u16_le_sum
checksum.algorithm: 16-bit little-endian additive sum of the frame payload bytes, mod 65536

fixtures.note: handshake hello/ack
get-catalog command (cmd 0x0110)

catalog/list response (cmd 0x0110); enumerated config/identity records because the recorded-session store was empty at capture time. Issue #133 established why: this phase was captured two minutes AFTER the transfer phase, by which point the app had imported and cleared the 44 sessions the transfer capture shows being downloaded.

one download data chunk. Issue #133 identified it from the same capture as chunk #2 of the track/config file 0:/tkk/al.ria (which the device serves uncompressed) — not session telemetry. Kept as the verbatim, observed-checksum wire anchor for the chunk framing.
SYNTHETIC (issue 6.6): the delete opcode was never captured (device held 0 sessions); frozen so build_delete_request is pinned byte-for-byte. Real capture tracked in issue #130 (PROTOCOL.md §7).
SYNTHETIC (issue 6.6): hypothesized delete-ack response — payload = status(u16 LE)=0 || session_id(u32 LE). Real capture tracked in issue #130.
SYNTHETIC (issue 6.6): hypothesized delete-reject response — payload = status(u16 LE)=1 || session_id(u32 LE). Real capture tracked in issue #130.
client read-file request (cmd 0x0402); payload[32..] is the NUL-terminated on-device path
device open ack (tag 0x0a09): echoes the path, declares no length

scrubbed: declared length re-stated after the session payload was de-identified
fixtures.note: device transfer header (tag 0x0a11): payload[16..20] = total length, payload[20..24] = 0xFFC0 chunk stride
client flow-control ACK: a bare u32 LE 'next offset' (here 65472)

issue #133: a whole captured session download (1:/mem/a_0053.xrz) as consecutive STCP chunk frames. The device's 4-byte identity word was replaced with 0x00000000 inside the session before it was re-deflated and re-framed, so the payload bytes are de-identified and the per-frame checksums are recomputed; every protocol field (framing, 0xFFC0 stride, offsets, short-final-chunk end-of-stream) is as observed. Originally 215325 B compressed.
client hello: payload 00000000 06 08 0000 (the device answers with control/hello.bin, 06 09)
device echo of the session-open command 0x0110 with tag 0x0a01 (ready to receive the client upload) and stride 0xFFC0 at payload[20..24]

client upload for 0x0110: offset(u32)=0, then 64 bytes = 8 zero bytes, local year/month/day/hour/minute/second (u32 LE each), 8 zero bytes, UTC year..second. Captured 2026-07-21 14:16:00 local / 11:16:00 UTC
device ack of the client upload: a bare u32 LE (observed 0)
device response header for 0x0110 (tag 0x0a11): payload[16..20] = 4268, the identity/path-table reply that follows (sessions/list_response.bin is that reply, de-identified)
client info read (cmd 0x0002) the AiM app issues after session-open; its reply is read and discarded
client info read (cmd 0x0008) the AiM app issues after session-open; its reply is read and discarded
client info read (cmd 0x0003) the AiM app issues after session-open; its reply is read and discarded
client catalog request (cmd 0x0224): the device answers with the download-summary CSV (1:/mem/dwnsm)
device echo of 0x0224 with tag 0x0a09
device response header for 0x0224 (tag 0x0a11): payload[16..20] = CSV length, re-stated for the de-identified CSV
scrubbed: declared length re-stated for the de-identified catalog

fixtures.note: the catalog reply: offset(u32)=0 + the download-summary CSV (header + one row per stored session). Cut to the 6 newest rows; track names, coordinates and driver replaced with FIXTURE placeholders
client close (cmd 0x0001, tag 0x0a00) sent when the AiM app disconnects; no reply observed

pending.reason: The real delete opcode + response are still uncaptured: the MyChron6 held 0 on-device sessions at 6.2 capture time (all imported to local), so no delete traffic could be observed. Issue 6.6 lands a guarded delete client over SYNTHETIC delete/*.bin fixtures (opcode + response shape hypothesized); a real on-the-wire delete must be captured to confirm them — tracked in issue #130.

The retry / re-request handshake is still unobserved: the session-present capture (issue #133) completed with zero chunk-checksum failures, so the device never had to re-send a chunk. Recovery remains exercised against synthetic streams in transfer_test.rs.

goldens.note: the .xrk a real device download yields; decodes to track 'S.Marino AR', 26 channels
